The paper establishes an analytical scattering method for radially anisotropic spherical cloaks with arbitrary radial-dependent permittivity and permeability.
The inhomogeneous cloak shell is discretized into N homogeneous anisotropic spherical layers for numerical computation.
The evolution operator Ω_r connects tangential electromagnetic fields at different radii within the cloak.
The general cloaking condition is expressed as Ω_b^a = [[0, 0], [-Γ^l(b), I]], independent of the inner core material parameters.
Zero scattering condition requires the scattered field amplitude H_lm(b) = 0 for all spherical harmonic modes.
The NTB cloak uses a nonlinear radial transformation r' = (b x + 1)/( (b - a)^x ) * (r - a)^x with nonlinearity parameter x ≥ 0.
Material parameters ε and µ of the NTB cloak are derived from the Jacobian of the nonlinear transformation and are radially anisotropic.
The cloak shell parameters satisfy ε_r = µ_r and ε_t = µ_t to ensure impedance matching.
The cloak shell is modeled as a multilayer structure to approximate continuous parameter variation.
Numerical results show that increasing the number of layers N improves approximation accuracy and reduces scattering.
The NTB cloak with optimized nonlinearity and core-shell ratio achieves better invisibility than Pendry's linear cloak.
Electric and magnetic fields vanish at the inner boundary of the cloak shell, ensuring no field penetration into the cloaked region.
The scattering cross-section is normalized by the geometric cross-section πb^2 for performance evaluation.
The spherical harmonics expansion is used to represent electromagnetic fields in the scattering problem.
The impedance tensor Γ_l relates electric and magnetic fields for each spherical harmonic mode and is key to boundary condition formulation.
The proposed scattering algorithm can handle arbitrary radial-dependent anisotropic parameters, extending beyond previous linear cloak models.
The cloak design is based on coordinate transformation invariance of Maxwell's equations.
The cloak's invisibility is robust against arbitrary materials inside the cloaked core.
The evolution operator is a degenerate block matrix with no inverse, reflecting the cloaking condition.
The paper provides a theoretical framework that can guide practical fabrication using multilayer metamaterial shells.
